races.title: State Senate, District 49
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: CJ Domingo
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 49 in 2026, running in the Asheville area against incumbent Julie Mayfield (D). No prior elected office or career history was found in the available pages.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Domingo was born or raised, when he came to North Carolina, or his career and work history. He has held no elected office that we could find. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. His campaign site gives general themes (infrastructure, Helene recovery, services, worker protection, transparency) but no specific positions on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, guns, abortion, policing or school choice, and no documented actions on any of them. We found no news coverage, controversies or foreign ties.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site says he would protect NC workers, farmers and families from the threat of massive job loss and would push employers to create career opportunities for people who live in the state. It does not mention H-1B or immigration enforcement.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says the state must provide for children's education, health and preparation for a post-AI NC. It names no vouchers, charters, school choice or teacher pay position, so this is only a loose fit.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

cands.name: Julie Mayfield
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina Senate for District 49 (Asheville area) since January 2021. Attorney and environmental advocate. Served on Asheville City Council from 2015 to 2020. Executive director of MountainTrue from 2008, later co-director and now senior policy advisor.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina endorsed her in 2026, per Ballotpedia.
Center for Freethought Equality endorsed her in 2026, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We found no documented position by her on data centers or on development and growth beyond her campaign statements. We found nothing on the homestead property tax, limits on out-of-state or institutional buyers of homes and land, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay and pensions, school choice, or teacher pay. We found no controversies and no foreign ties. The Issues page on her campaign site was cut off partway through, so anything below the "Giving Working Families A Fair Shot" section went unread. Her statements about her own votes and bills come from her campaign site and could not be checked against official records here.

local.label: Roots 40: She was born and raised in Atlanta and moved to North Carolina as an adult in 2008, about 18 years ago, though her campaign site says her mother's family has roots in Western North Carolina going back more than 150 years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since 2021 and Asheville City Council member (elected 2015, served five years). Environmental attorney and policy advocate for about 25 years: Kilpatrick Stockton associate, Emory environmental law clinic director, Georgia Conservancy general counsel, and MountainTrue executive director.
qual.why: She has prior legislative service in the state Senate and local elected office, plus a law and policy career, which fits the high range for writing law and the state budget.
qual.label: She has prior legislative service in the state Senate and local elected office, plus a law and policy career, which fits the high range for writing law and the state budget.

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says she voted against the abortion ban and describes an "all-out assault on women's rights" in North Carolina. This is her own description; the roll call was not checked.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site lists gun control among the issues she has been an outspoken proponent of.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her campaign bio says she chaired the Asheville council committees on affordable housing and planning and backed land use planning that will better manage the city's growth.
